issues.body: `no_change_census` filters out every record whose `exit_class` is not `no_change` before selecting the latest attempt per base run id. For a retained sequence such as `117.1 = no_change` followed by `117.2 = success`, attempt 2 is discarded and attempt 1 remains in `latest`, so the run is still counted as having left the tree unchanged even though its final execution produced a diff. This contradicts the documented one-vote-per-run/latest-outcome semantics and can falsely sustain `worker-no-change`. The added rerun fixture uses two no-change records, so it stays green through this bug.
issues.fix_hint: Select the latest attributable record per base run id across all validated exit classes first, then include that run in the census only when the selected record's `exit_class` is `no_change`. Add non-vacuous transition tests for `no_change -> success` (must not count) and `success -> no_change` (must count), with attempt order opposed to ledger order as appropriate.
issues.title: A successful rerun cannot supersede an earlier no-change attempt

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The prior denominator mismatch is addressed by folding records to one vote per GitHub run, but the fold is applied only after non-no-change outcomes have been discarded. Consequently, a later successful rerun cannot supersede an earlier no-change attempt: the run remains charged as no-change and can falsely sustain the new alert. The new rerun test covers only two no-change attempts, so it does not exercise this outcome transition.
